newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Superconductor sees $10-15 mln from placement.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Superconductor sees $10-15 mln from placement.

text.p: Illinois Superconductor Corp said Tuesday it expects to complete a private placement within the next 30 days that will provide it with $10-$15 million in operating capital.

The company said it expects the funding to enable it to execute its business plan for at least the next 12 to 15 months, including an "aggressive expansion" of sales and marketing activities for its wireless telephone system filters.
Illinois Superconductor said it is in final negotiations with a single financial partner for the private placement.
On May 9 the company said it had withdrawn a filing for a public stock offering. It cited conditions in the small-capitalization sector of the equity markets.

Ora Smith, Illinois Superconductor president and chief executive, said in a statement that the company is gaining critical sales momentum. He said orders for its SpectrumMaster and RangeMaster products have surpassed $1 million since the product line was introduced in late 1996. The filters enhance call quality and increase the capacity of wireless phone systems.
Smith said that because of the performance of the filters, the company has received follow-on orders from three customers who are among the top nine U.S. cellular phone operators.
Illinois Superconductor provides high-temperature superconducting technology for the wireless telecommunications industry.
